title: At the gym
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in general surgery. At your local gym, Mr Webb, a patient you consented for a hernia repair last week, recognises you.

He starts asking about his post-operative pain and shows you his wound in the changing room.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Examine his wound in the changing room.
options.detailed: This is not a clinical setting, and there's no privacy.

options.text: Advise him on painkillers there and then.
options.detailed: You don't know his history or current medications.
This avoids the situation, but may upset him.

options.text: Explain politely that you can't advise him properly here.
options.brief: A gym isn't a place for clinical advice.
options.detailed: You don't have his notes, can't examine him properly, and others may overhear. Explaining this kindly respects him.

options.text: Give him your phone number so he can contact you with questions.
options.detailed: This creates an informal relationship outside proper channels.

options.text: Suggest he contacts the ward, his GP or NHS 111 about his pain.
options.detailed: These services can assess him properly.

options.text: Discuss his operation with him in front of others in the changing room.
Be friendly, and wish him well with his recovery.
options.detailed: Being friendly, while keeping boundaries, is appropriate.

explanation.issue: This tests how you handle a patient seeking advice outside the clinical setting, keeping boundaries while being kind.
explanation.keyDetails: You're at the gym. He's in pain and wants advice. Others are present.
explanation.reasoning: [D] explains the limits, [F] directs him to help, and [H] stays friendly. The distractors give care inappropriately ([A], [B], [G]), avoid him ([C]), or blur boundaries ([E]).
explanation.competing: [B] may seem helpful, but you can't safely advise without proper assessment.
